hero.headline: BELLINGHAM AGAIN. MESSI MARCHES ON.
hero.standfirst: Jude Bellingham dragged England past Haaland's Norway with a brace finished three minutes into extra time — and hours later, ten-man Switzerland finally broke in Kansas City as Argentina won 3–1 in extra time of their own. The last four is a collector's edition: France–Spain, then England–Argentina.
hero.photoCaption: Jude Bellingham — an equaliser on the stroke of half-time, the winner in extra time

briefing.text: Crystal Ball, day five: England 2–1 was the call, England 2–1 the result — our second exact scoreline. Five winners from seven.
The early semi-final money: France 43% against Spain's 30 — and England–Argentina opens almost dead even (38–32).
Rest days today and tomorrow. Semi-final 1 is Tuesday in Dallas, semi-final 2 Wednesday in Atlanta — both at 21:00 our time.

insideToday.text: Norway 1–2 England (aet) — Bellingham's double ends Haaland's dream
Argentina 3–1 Switzerland (aet) — the champions outlast the Swiss wall
The semi-finals: France–Spain and England–Argentina, previewed

The bracket: four teams, seven days, one trophy

facts.text: Bellingham's winner came three minutes into extra time, pouncing when Nyland spilled Rogers' shot
Haaland was held without a goal for the first time in the knockouts — his tournament ends on 7
England reach a World Cup semi-final having trailed in both of their last two knockout ties

yesterday.report: For an hour, the fairy tale had legs. Andreas Schjelderup's 36th-minute cross-shot caught everyone — including possibly himself — by surprise, and Norway's block did to England what it did to Brazil. But on the stroke of half-time Jude Bellingham found the equaliser his tournament deserved, and the game slid towards the extra half-hour both sets of legs feared.
yesterday.report2: Three minutes into it, Ørjan Nyland spilled Morgan Rogers' drive and Bellingham reacted first — his fourth goal of the tournament, and the end of Norway's greatest World Cup. Haaland, marked by a crowd all night, never got his chance. England march into Wednesday's semi-final in Atlanta having twice come from behind to survive.

star.name: Jude Bellingham
star.line: Twice at the Azteca, twice more in Miami. Four goals, every one of them in a knockout game England were losing or drawing. Big-game player is no longer a debate.

aside.name: Erling Haaland
aside.line: Held quiet on the night it mattered, but he leaves with 7 goals, a nation's first quarter-final, and the tournament's most terrifying highlight reel.

yesterday.whatItMeans: England meet Argentina in Wednesday's Atlanta semi-final — a rematch of legends. Norway go home with the whole country's head held high.

events.text: Red card: Embolo (SUI), second bookable offence — the turning point of extra time

facts.text: Switzerland's wall held Argentina level for over 100 minutes before Embolo's second yellow broke the dam
Álvarez struck in the 112th minute, Lautaro sealed it — the champions' third extra-time escape of the knockouts
Argentina have now come from level or behind in every knockout game — and won them all

yesterday.report: Kansas City got the siege everyone predicted, just longer. Alexis Mac Allister's first-half opener should have settled Argentine nerves, but Dan Ndoye's equaliser after the hour dragged the champions into a familiar place: level, late, and staring at penalties against the team that knocked out Colombia exactly that way.
yesterday.report2: Then Breel Embolo's second yellow tilted the pitch. Against ten men, Julián Álvarez finally beat Kobel in the 112th minute and Lautaro Martínez added the third before the end. Argentina's knockout run now reads like a stress test passed three times — and Wednesday brings England, in a rematch of one of football's oldest arguments.

star.name: Lionel Messi
star.line: No goal this time, but 120 more minutes of steering the champions through a storm at 39. Two games stand between him and a second consecutive World Cup.

aside.name: Gregor Kobel
aside.line: Beaten only in the deep minutes of extra time after another towering night. Switzerland's revival ends, but their goalkeeper leaves as one of the tournament's names.

yesterday.whatItMeans: England–Argentina in Wednesday's Atlanta semi-final. Switzerland's first quarter-final in 72 years ends with pride fully intact.

todaySub: Rest days today and Monday — then two nights that decide the final

today.preview: The final arriving early. France are the tournament's only perfect team — seven wins, never extra time, Mbappé and Dembélé combining for 13 goals. Spain conceded their first goal of the whole tournament on Friday and still won, with super-sub Merino striking late for the second time in a week. The early market leans French: 43% to 30, with a big 30% on the draw.
watch: Mbappé v Spain's record defence — 8 goals against 1 conceded all tournament
Merino, the bench weapon Spain now openly plan around
The winner gets six days' rest before the MetLife final

keyMan.name: Kylian Mbappé
keyMan.line: Eight goals, level with Messi, and the one attacking force no defence has held. Spain's is the last wall standing between him and a third final.

today.preview: 1986 and the Hand of God, 1998 and Beckham's red, 2002 and Beckham's penalty — England–Argentina needs no introduction, and now it decides a World Cup semi-final. Both sides needed extra time on Saturday; both have made comebacks their identity. The market can barely split them: England 38%, Argentina 32%, the draw 32%.
watch: Bellingham against Messi — the tournament's man of the moment against its eternal one
Kane (5 goals) quietly hunting the Golden Boot leaders
Both teams played 120 minutes Saturday — the fresher legs may decide it

keyMan.name: Lionel Messi
keyMan.line: At 39, two games from retaining the World Cup. England are the only historic rival his trophy cabinet is still missing an answer to.
